subject: Capacity sculpting & phased onramp offer — SolsticeAI dedicated cluster options
messages:
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Priya Desai <priya.desai@solstice.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity sculpting & phased onramp offer — SolsticeAI dedicated cluster options

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday — really excited about the work SolsticeAI is planning. Per our ask, attached is a compact set of dedicated reservation alternatives designed to match a typical ML inference ramp while keeping unit cost predictable as you scale. The attachments are: capacity_sculpting_offer_v1.pdf and Solstice_Demand_Forecast.xlsx.

High level summary (three options):

Option A — Conservative baseline
- Cluster: 8x A100-equivalent GPUs (single pool)
- Minimum guarantee: 4 GPUs sustained
- Ramp: weeks 1–6: 4 -> 8 GPUs (linear weekly increases)
- Burst windows: +50% queued burst for 4 hours/day during business-critical hours
- Warm-up credits: 50k tokens/month for first 3 months
- Use case: PoC -> limited-prod usage, lowest monthly commit

Option B — Production steady-state (recommended)
- Cluster: 24x A100-equivalent GPUs (sharded pools for chat & embeddings)
- Minimum guarantee: 12 GPUs sustained
- Ramp: weeks 1–12: 12 -> 24 GPUs (milestone-linked triggers)
- Burst windows: +25% across region with prioritized routing to reduce latency spikes
- Warm-up credits: 200k tokens/month for first 2 months
- Use case: initial production, predictable latency & throughput

Option C — Aggressive growth (enterprise throughput)
- Cluster: 48x A100-equivalent GPUs (multi-queue architecture)
- Minimum guarantee: 24 GPUs sustained
- Ramp: quarter 1: 24 -> 48 GPUs (phased monthly activations)
- Burst windows: flexibility for geo-bursting + pre-warm lanes for peak events
- Warm-up credits: 500k tokens + 1 wake-up run of model warm cache
- Use case: high-throughput customer-facing workloads with SLAs

Operational notes:
- We recommend Option B for the use case you described — it balances cost predictability and headroom for model experimentation.
- Autoscale policy: we can configure a soft autoscale that allows temporary bursts beyond the min GPU guarantee while counting to committed baseline.
- Fallback model variants: if capacity is constrained, requests will be routed to compatible quantized variants with a measurable latency/cost delta.

Next steps / asks:
1) Can you confirm target peak qps and percent of requests that require >2k context? That feeds the queuing model in the spreadsheet.
2) Procurement timeline — are you aiming to sign within 30/60/90 days?
3) Any compliance constraints (region, KMS) we should bake into the Private deployment option?

I'll follow up with a short version of the commercial terms and a draft SLA (SLA_Draft.docx). Happy to jump on a call with Karthik to walk the technical side.

Best,
Dev
Lead Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: capacity_sculpting_offer_v1.pdf (7 pages), Solstice_Demand_Forecast.xlsx (3 sheets)

From: Priya Desai <priya.desai@solstice.ai>

Date: Tue, 25 May 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity sculpting & phased onramp offer — SolsticeAI dedicated cluster options

Hi Dev —

Appreciate the crisp set of options and the forecast. Quick questions from our side after a quick pass (we'll review the spreadsheet in detail this afternoon):

1) Minimums: for Option B, is the 12-GPU sustained guarantee measured as average across the month or strict concurrent count? We need to map that to our SLA with clients.
2) Credits and warm-up: how are those consumed/tracked? Can we get visibility in the Console per-route?
3) Procurement & billing cadence: we typically prefer quarterly billing tied to usage over commit with a soft-commit overlay. Is that supported?
4) Security: we plan to keep data in a US region and use our KMS. Any gotchas for Private control plane deployment?

Timeline: procurement wants a commercial summary this week; legal will want your SLA draft and a short doc on data residency/KMS integration. Can Marissa and Karthik coordinate the technical appendix?

Thanks —
Priya
VP Engineering, SolsticeAI

(On a related note — we may run a high-traffic pilot for two weeks in July; if we go with Option B, we'll likely ask for an abbreviated burst credit so that we don't hit throttles.)

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Priya Desai <priya.desai@solstice.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 26 May 2026 14:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity sculpting & phased onramp offer — SolsticeAI dedicated cluster options

Hi Priya — thanks, good questions. Answers inline below and a short operational plan.

1) Minimums (Option B): the 12-GPU guarantee is a sustained concurrent capacity measured at 5-minute sampling windows averaged across the month for billing/commit accounting. You can enable soft buffers for a short period — those are billed against the committed baseline if sustained beyond the threshold.

2) Credits & visibility: warm-up and burst credits are tracked as separate line items in Redwood Console. We provide route-level token consumption and a token-credits ledger export for audit. I'll attach a sample Console export after this thread.

3) Billing cadence: we support quarterly invoicing for enterprise customers with a soft-commit overlay. The soft-commit lets you exceed baseline for short periods (with overage rates) and we reconcile usage against commit at the cadence you prefer. Commercials will reflect a small discount for quarterly prepay vs monthly metered.

4) Security/KMS: Private control plane with customer-managed KMS is supported in our US region. The main caveat is if you want HSM-backed keys in an air-gapped on-prem packaging — that requires an additional compliance review and a 2–3 week lead time. For standard customer-managed KMS in cloud, we have turnkey integrations documented in the attached SLA_Draft.docx.

Operational plan (proposed timeline):
- Week 0 (sign): Kickoff, allocate pool, reserve minimum 12 GPUs (Option B baseline)
- Weeks 1–4: Warm-start — deploy model, populate KV cache, run throughput validation with low-traffic ramp (we'll provide 200k warm-up tokens)
- Weeks 5–12: Linear activation to 24 GPUs tied to milestone checks (latency < 300ms p95 on chat flows, throughput targets)
- July 15–28: Pilot burst window (2-week run) — we can isolate a warm-lane for that pilot; request this be flagged in procurement to secure burst lanes

Docs & links: HubSpot deal (https://hubspot.redwood.com/deals/78321), proposal folder (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-solstice-capacity).

Next steps:
- Marissa: can you share the commercial summary (numbers for Option B with quarterly billing) so Priya's procurement can review this week?
- Karthik: can you prepare the short technical appendix on KMS integration and the 5-min sampling definition?

I'll hold a 30-minute slot tomorrow to walk through the timeline if that helps.

Thanks —
Dev

Attachments: SLA_Draft.docx (3 pages)
